title: The guard refuses Edit and Write in the pointer checkout
why: A lane edited the shared pointer checkout that other sessions read; guard pointer-head stopped only its branch switch, not the edits.
note: Coordinator, 04:28 CST Nov 9. Incident: lane fresh-round3-route (#2411) edited the pointer checkout first; guard pointer-head refused only the branch switch. Harm: edits land in a shared checkout that other sessions read. Unassigned; the coordinator routes it after batch 68. Batch 68 merged (#2449, 11:55 CST Nov 9): free to start. Lane [ended:Lane-pointer-checkout-edit] started 12:13 CST Nov 9 (coordinator). Done: on main by #2456, 247aab76a (coordinator's Explore agent (Sonnet) read of origin/main 0e6509a96, 05:01 CST Nov 10). Reopened, triage 21:08 CST Nov 12 (coordinator sighting 21:01 CST): lane decision-watch-finds-transcript (session_013NEJL1SWvL24cv7TG6nxAT, #3054) edited hooks/decision_watch.py and its test in the pointer checkout /home/user/claude-settings, then moved to a worktree; restore was refused by other-checkout. The coordinator wrote that pointer-head fires only on a branch switch. Triage read of origin/main: rule pointer-edit (guard.py, refuse "pointer-edit"; guard_pointer.pointer_edit_hit) refuses Edit and Write there since #2456, and the live hook copy in this container has it. So the edit got past a live guard. The lane finds how: a Bash write (sed, python, heredoc) that WRITE_TOOLS does not cover, an earlier allow in guard.py, or a pointer path that pointer_checkout() did not resolve in that container. Then it closes that path, red then green. Harm: a lane builds in the shared checkout and leaves it dirty. Coordinator 21:05 CST Nov 12: started, lane session_013NEJL1xN2nGvUxowmqV5uk.
